parts.visual:
When a manager wants to fire someone but doesn't want to pay severance, they sometimes try to make the employee's life so miserable that they quit voluntarily. This is illegal.

The Concept:
1. Constructive Dismissal: Changing an employee's job so drastically (e.g., cutting their pay by 50%, moving their office to the basement) that they are forced to resign.
2. The Lawsuit: The law treats a forced resignation exactly the same as an unjust firing.
parts.audio: Trying to make an employee quit by making their life miserable is illegal. It is called Constructive Dismissal, and the law treats it exactly like a wrongful termination.

questions.question: A VP wants to fire an executive, but the executive has a $1 Million severance clause. The VP decides to take away all of the executive's direct reports and demote them to a junior desk, hoping they will quit out of shame. What will happen?
options: The executive will quit and get nothing.
The executive will quit, immediately sue the company for 'Constructive Dismissal', and win the $1 Million plus damages.
questions.correct_answer: The executive will quit, immediately sue the company for 'Constructive Dismissal', and win the $1 Million plus damages.
questions.explanation: Judges are not stupid. They recognize when a resignation is actually a disguised firing.

questions.question: Listen to the HR Director. What mistake is the manager making?
questions.tts_text: You cannot suddenly force the marketing director to work the night shift in the warehouse just because you don't like her. That is a massive legal liability.
questions.explanation: Fundamentally altering the core duties or conditions of an employment contract without consent is illegal.

questions.question: How should a professional executive handle a highly-paid employee who is underperforming?
options: Put them on a formal Performance Improvement Plan (PIP). If they fail the PIP after 60 days, fire them cleanly and legally.
questions.correct_answer: Put them on a formal Performance Improvement Plan (PIP). If they fail the PIP after 60 days, fire them cleanly and legally.
questions.explanation: A PIP creates a documented paper trail proving that the firing was based on performance, not discrimination or malice.

questions.question: What is 'At-Will Employment' in the United States?
options: You only work when you want to.
A legal doctrine stating an employer can fire an employee for any reason, with no warning—as long as the reason isn't illegal (like race, gender, or retaliation).
questions.correct_answer: A legal doctrine stating an employer can fire an employee for any reason, with no warning—as long as the reason isn't illegal (like race, gender, or retaliation).
questions.explanation: While 'At-Will' gives employers power, firing someone without documentation often invites brutal discrimination lawsuits.

pairs.match: Changing a job so drastically that the employee is forced to resign
An employer's right to terminate an employee at any time for any legal reason
Compensation paid to an employee whose employment has been terminated
